key_insight: An extensible membrane in inviscid flow can be modeled with a weak Galerkin formulation that remains usable at vanishing bending rigidity, revealing how fluid loading, vortex shedding, and tension degeneracy control lift, wrinkles, and flutter transitions.
engineering_relevance: The results inform the design of lightweight flexible structures by showing when compliance improves start-up lift, when it mainly increases unsteady loads, and how free edges can trigger rapid tip-snapping and instability.
method: 2D inviscid fluid–structure interaction model with continuous vortex shedding from both edges
Weak spectral Galerkin discretization of the membrane equation to handle zero bending rigidity
Analysis of fixed-fixed and free-trailing-edge cases, including singular limits and flutter dynamics
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct computation across rigid and singular limits and identifies observed behaviors such as delayed vortex detachment, wrinkle formation, inverse-logarithmic frequency corrections, and destabilization to chaotic flutter as stretching modulus decreases.
watch_item: The free-edge, zero-bending case is formally underdetermined unless the weak bounded-energy branch is selected, so numerical implementations must carefully enforce the correct variational limit.
paper_title: Extensible membranes in inviscid flow: aerodynamics and singular limits
